$comment: The review rail's Jev questions (compiled-prompts D2) — exactly what askJev sends, plus `measured`. Loaded by lib/review-guard.mjs. A recording pins each question by hash (D3): change a word and `node scripts/jev-eval.mjs` fails until `--live` re-records. A new wording is measured on held-out folds before it is proposed (in the golden-frijoles monorepo: optimize/wording.mjs).

questions.instructions: This is the output of an automated code reviewer. Did the reviewer deliver a verdict on the change?

criteria.true: Yes: it reports at least one finding about the code, OR it states a verdict that there is nothing to fix — e.g. "Clean.", "No findings.", "Blocking: None. Should-fix: None.", "Diff looks clean." A short clean verdict counts, and boilerplate footers after it do not change that.
criteria.false: No: the reviewer did not finish or never started — empty severity headings, a timeout or "analysis incomplete" note, a quota, rate-limit, login or HTTP error, a CLI banner or help text, a preamble or plan saying what it will do, or a raw tool-call transcript.

measured.how: offline replay of the 77 labelled review fixtures in jev-eval.fixtures.json through judgeReviewOutput at real ≥ 0.85 / not-real ≤ 0.3; decided = Jev decided (outside the band, where the regex decides); right = decided and matches the label.

questions.instructions: What is the most severe finding this review reports?

criteria.blocking: At least one finding the reviewer says must be fixed before merge (a bug, a broken contract, a security hole).
criteria.should_fix: Nothing blocking, but at least one finding the reviewer says should be fixed.
criteria.clean: No findings: the reviewer says the change is clean, or reports nothing to fix.

questions.unmeasured: No labelled severities exist: it is logged beside the verdict and decides nothing.
